question: How does Schwab utilize its scale to cheaply acquire new clients and how could Edward Jones replicate a similar strategy?

claims.text: Schwab: Schwab states that its operating efficiency, coupled with scale and sharing of infrastructure across businesses, creates a cost advantage enabling competitive pricing while profitably serving clients across channels.

Schwab: Schwab states its scale, combined with expense discipline, decreased its cost per account 20% over the last five years, driving industry leadership in expense on client assets per Schwab's 4Q25 call (period ended December 31, 2025).
Schwab: Schwab states its marketing spend drives approximately 40% of new-to-firm retail clients per its 1Q25 call (period ended March 31, 2025).
Schwab: Schwab states that 90% of accounts are opened digitally as of September 30, 2026, and that it leverages its scale to maintain a structural cost advantage while continuing to invest in growth.
Schwab: Schwab states that in 2025 about half of new-to-firm retail clients initiated access to its thinkorswim platform.

Schwab: Schwab cites scale and size of the business as a competitive advantage, stating that as one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., it can spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients (10-K, fiscal 2025).

Schwab: Schwab cites its operating efficiency coupled with scale and sharing of infrastructure across businesses as creating a cost advantage that enables competitive pricing of products and services across multiple channels (10-K, fiscal 2025).

Schwab: CEO Rick Wurster cites Schwab's transfer of assets ratio of 1.5 as evidence it wins clients and assets from competitors, meaning every dollar that leaves Schwab is met with $1.50 coming from competitors.
Schwab: Schwab cites multiple growth levers across its leading platform, including winning new clients across Retail, Advisor Services, and Workplace channels (investor day deck, May 2026).

Schwab: Schwab states it is winning with younger investors and traders, with one in six new-to-firm retail households under age 24, more than 30% of new-to-firm clients under age 30, and nearly 60% under age 40 (2Q25 call, June 2025).
Schwab: Schwab states approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials (3Q26 call, period ended September 30, 2026).

Schwab: Schwab states that for self-directed clients it provides digital and software-based trading platforms, real-time market data, research tools, and multichannel support, with Schwab Trading Powered by Ameritrade offering the thinkorswim suite and specialized education and 24/7 support (10-K, fiscal 2025).
Schwab: Schwab reported core net new assets of $366.9 billion in 2024, up 20% from 2023, an annualized growth rate of 4.3% (10-K, fiscal 2025).
Schwab: Schwab reported clients opened 4.2 million new brokerage accounts in 2024, up 10% year-over-year (10-K, fiscal 2025).
Schwab: Schwab reported active brokerage accounts of 36.5 million at the end of 2024, up 5% on the year (10-K, fiscal 2025).
Schwab: Schwab reported core net new assets of $519.4 billion for 2025, up 42% from the prior year, an annualized organic growth rate of 5.1% (10-K, fiscal 2025).
Schwab: Schwab reported 4.7 million new brokerage accounts opened in 2025, up 13% from the prior year (10-K, fiscal 2025).
Schwab: Schwab reported active brokerage accounts of 38.5 million as of December 31, 2025, up 6% from year-end 2024 (10-K, fiscal 2025).
Schwab: Schwab reported core net new assets of $137.7 billion for the first quarter of 2025 (10-Q, 1Q26, Item 2).
Schwab: Schwab reported core net new assets of $80.3 billion in the second quarter of 2025, up 31% year-over-year (10-Q, 2Q25).
Schwab: Schwab reported year-to-date core net new assets of $218.0 billion for the first half of 2025, up 39% from the first half of 2024 (10-Q, 2Q25).
Schwab: Schwab reported clients opened 1.1 million new brokerage accounts in the second quarter of 2025, up 11% year-over-year (10-Q, 2Q25).
Schwab: Schwab reported core net new assets of $137.5 billion in the third quarter of 2025, up 44% year-over-year (10-Q, 3Q25).
Schwab: Schwab reported core net new assets of $355.5 billion for the first nine months of 2025, up 41% year-over-year (10-Q, 3Q25).
Schwab: Schwab reported clients opened 1.1 million new brokerage accounts in the third quarter of 2025, up 18% year-over-year (10-Q, 3Q25).
Schwab: Schwab reported record fourth-quarter core net new assets of $163.9 billion, bringing total 2025 asset gathering to $519.4 billion (press release, January 21, 2026).

Schwab: Schwab reported core net new assets of $140.0 billion in the first quarter of 2026, up 2% year-over-year, including a $17.5 billion outflow from a planned mutual fund clearing client deconversion (10-Q, 1Q26, Item 2).
Schwab: Schwab reported clients opened 1.3 million new brokerage accounts in the first quarter of 2026, up 10% from the prior-year first quarter (10-Q, 1Q26, Item 2).
Schwab: Schwab reported core net new assets of $119.8 billion in the second quarter of 2026, up 49% from the same period in 2025 (10-Q, 2Q26).
Schwab: Schwab reported core net new assets of $259.8 billion for the first half of 2026, up 19% from the first half of 2025 (10-Q, 2Q26).
Schwab: Schwab reported new brokerage accounts of 1.4 million and 2.7 million in the second quarter and first half of 2026, respectively, up 26% and 18% year-over-year (10-Q, 2Q26).
Schwab: Schwab reported clients opened 1.2 million brokerage accounts in the third quarter of 2026 and attracted $190 billion in core net new assets, up 38% over last year (3Q26 call, October 2026).

Edward Jones: Edward Jones acquires and serves clients through its branch office model, designed to serve clients through deep, personal relationships and comprehensive advice and planning with financial advisors and client support team professionals located in the communities where clients live and work (10-K, fiscal 2025).

Edward Jones: Edward Jones targets new clients through initiatives including High Net Worth, Workplace, and a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors (10-K, fiscal 2025).

Edward Jones: Edward Jones's operating expenses increased 11% to $15,610 million in 2025, primarily due to increases in compensation and benefits expense, variable compensation, and communications and data processing expense (10-K, fiscal 2025).

Edward Jones: Edward Jones's income before allocations was $2,090 million in 2025 with an 11.7% margin, which the firm describes as reflecting a strategic balance between investing in the future and current financial results (10-K, fiscal 2025).

Edward Jones: Edward Jones's financial advisor compensation and benefits expense increased 12% to $6,969 million in 2025, primarily due to increases in revenues on which commissions are earned (10-K, fiscal 2025).

Edward Jones: Edward Jones's variable compensation increased 11% to $2,710 million in 2025, which the firm describes as expanding and contracting in relation to the Partnership's profitability and margin earned (10-K, fiscal 2025).

Edward Jones: Edward Jones's communications and data processing expense increased 16% to $1,162 million in 2025, primarily due to continued investments in new tools and technology and higher depreciation expense (10-K, fiscal 2025).
Edward Jones: Edward Jones's advertising expense was $43 million in the first quarter of 2026, compared with $39 million in the first quarter of 2025 (10-Q, 1Q26, Item 2).

Edward Jones: Edward Jones's existing client-serving model is its branch office network, designed to serve clients through deep, personal relationships and comprehensive advice and planning (10-K, fiscal 2025).

Edward Jones: Edward Jones's stated strategic ambition includes continuing to invest in technology to scale its ability to provide financial planning to clients, and to attract and serve new client segments (10-K, fiscal 2025).

Edward Jones: Edward Jones's initiatives for targeting new clients include High Net Worth, Workplace, and a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors (10-K, fiscal 2025).

Edward Jones: Trade press reports that Edward Jones has taken a minority stake in the personal finance app Quicken, with the stated intention of integrating Quicken's personal financial management capabilities more directly into Edward Jones to support its value proposition and advisor conversations with clients, though the firm notes it is still determining the actual deployment strategy (trade press, August 18, 2026).

Edward Jones: Trade press reports that Edward Jones is integrating a technology platform (RPMC, leveraging Aboon Workplace) into its advisor workstation that will cover the entire workplace retirement plan lifecycle, from prospecting to plan servicing, with a prospecting module currently in beta and expected to go live to the broader network early next year (trade press, September 30, 2026).

Whether and how Edward Jones could replicate Schwab's scale-based low-cost client acquisition strategy cannot be determined on this evidence: the question asks for a normative recommendation, which is beyond what the cited sources state. The evidence shows each firm's own statements about its acquisition approach, but neither firm states how the other could replicate its strategy.

adjacent.text: Schwab: Schwab reports that GAAP cost per client account was $442 in 2020, calculated as total expenses excluding interest divided by average active brokerage accounts (investor relations deck, 2Q26, p.17).
adjacent.differs_because: GAAP cost per client account is a cost-efficiency measure across the whole client base, not a disclosed client acquisition cost per new client.

adjacent.text: Schwab: Schwab states that its cost per client account has decreased more than 25% in the last decade (4Q24 call, as of January 2025).
adjacent.differs_because: Cost per client account is a cost-to-serve all clients measure, not a disclosed client acquisition cost per new client.

adjacent.text: Schwab: Schwab states that its scale combined with expense discipline has decreased cost per account 20% over the last five years (4Q25 call, as of January 2026).
adjacent.differs_because: Cost per account is a cost-to-serve measure, not a disclosed client acquisition cost per new client.

adjacent.text: Schwab: Schwab states it has improved cost per account by more than 20% over the last decade (1Q25 call, as of April 2025).
adjacent.differs_because: Cost per account is a cost-to-serve measure, not a disclosed client acquisition cost per new client.

gaps.what: Schwab does not disclose a client acquisition cost or cost-per-new-client figure; the closest disclosed figures are cost per client account figures (latest is 2020), which measure cost-to-serve, not cost of acquisition.
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab investor relations materials, earnings transcripts, or regulatory filings with an explicit client acquisition cost or cost per new client metric

gaps.what: Edward Jones does not disclose a cost-per-new-client figure or an acquisition cost structure directly comparable to Schwab's scale-based figures.
gaps.suggested_source: Edward Jones regulatory filings or earnings materials with an explicit client acquisition cost metric
